question: Romania and Bulgaria will join Schengen as regards air and sea borders in March 2024, with a separate decision on accession as regards land and river borders to be discussed at a later stage. Tens of thousands of Romanian hauliers are suffering huge financial losses and are being humiliated in having to spend hours and even days at border crossing points.

Given the situation in which Romanian carriers find themselves, I would like to ask the Commission whether it is considering allocating funds to compensate transport companies and hauliers for the financial losses suffered due to the situation at the borders with the Schengen area?
The creation of a European Road Transport Agency would help harmonise and strengthen oversight of road transport operations with a view to implementing social and road safety legislation in Europe.

There is a need for EU-level supervision of road transport in order to apply the relevant social and road safety legislation, and such EU-level supervision could be achieved more effectively through the intermediary of a European Road Transport Agency. Does the Commission plan to create such an agency at EU level?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.4.2024) The Commission fully supports the swift completion of the process of admission of Bulgaria and Romania to the Schengen area without controls at internal borders, in particular as regards the lifting of checks at its land borders1.

The Commission will continue to provide all necessary support to the Presidency to ensure that a decision on land borders can be taken this year. This will contribute to eliminating barriers within the single market, such as excessive waiting times at border crossing points, thus facilitating transport flows and fostering EU’s competitiveness and growth potential.

The Commission has no available budgetary appropriations which would allow to compensate Bulgarian and Romanian hauliers for possible financial losses suffered due to the situation at the borders with the Schengen area.

The Commission committed under Action 40 of the Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy2 to ‘explore the options to further support safe, smart and sustainable road transport operations under an existing agency or another body’.

In this context, the Commission recalls that the European Labour Authority (ELA), EU agency established in 2019, contributes, among others, to the implementation and enforcement of EU legislation in the road transport sector with regard to cross-border labour mobility and social security aspects.

In this field, the ELA coordinates and supports crossborder checks with joint and concerted inspections both at the roadside and at the premises of undertakings, promotes a common understanding of EU social legislation and the exchange of practices, with a view to strengthening the cooperation between Member States.
1 On 30 December 2023 the Council took a historic decision on the accession of Bulgaria and Romania to the

Schengen area: from 31 March 2024, Bulgaria and Romania will start to fully apply the Schengen acquis and any person, irrespective of their nationality, will as of that date be able to cross the internal air and maritime borders between Romania and Bulgaria and the other Schengen Member States, and between themselves, without being subjected to border checks: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?

uri=OJ:L_202400210 The Council agreed that a further decision should be taken at an appropriate date for the lifting of checks at internal land borders, which will for now be currently maintained between the land borders of Romania and Bulgaria and other Schengen Member States, as well as between Romania and Bulgaria. 2 COM(2020) 789 final.
